HOW TO FIND A PROMPT
  Search for the code with the bar after it, e.g. "GI 07 |", "No. 076 |", "OC 03 |". That lands on the entry
  itself instead of the index. Search "PART 4 |" to jump to a whole part.

HOW EACH PROMPT IS LAID OUT
  Line 1   your quality block, ending in "safe"
  BREAK    character tag (canon characters) or species tag (originals), then expression, eyes, hair, horns,
           ears and hair ornaments
  BREAK    non-human body features - only when there are any (scales, wings, tails, extra eyes, stitches)
  BREAK    camera angle + outfit and accessories
  BREAK    pose, weapon and props
  BREAK    background, framing and body type, then your style and artist tail

NOTES THAT APPLY EVERYWHERE
- Every quality line now ends in "safe". Before the merge the FGO, Unicorn Overlord and Stardew Valley
  prompts did not have it.
- There are two quality lines: the full one, and a shorter one without "skin texture, soft lips, smooth skin,
  glossy skin" for kids, the elderly, child-like characters and creatures, where those tags fight the subject.
- Canon prompts start with the character's tag plus the series. Brackets inside tags are escaped with
  backslashes so A1111, Forge and ComfyUI do not read them as weights.
- Backgrounds are white unless the entry has its own scene (Part 1). Swap in a scene if you want one.
- Adult men get "maleT"; slim men, kids and the elderly do not.
- Every part has the expanded, high-detail descriptions (about 2-3x the original length). Parts 1 and 2 were
  expanded freely; Parts 3-8 (game characters) only gained design details where the official look is well known.
- A BREAK section longer than about 75 tokens spills into a second chunk. That works, but tags late in a very
  long section pull less weight, so the most important tags stay at the front of each line.

PART 2 | FANTASY ORIGINAL CHARACTERS | OC 01-15 | 15 prompts
//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
15 original characters: 2 dragonnewts, a demoness, a saintess, a cardinal, an inquisitor, 5 elves, 2 demi-humans,
a mermaid and a lamia.
- Species tag comes first (dragon girl, demon girl, cat girl...). Scales, wings and tails get their own BREAK.
- No gender was given for the inquisitor, elf, wood elf, dark elf, cat or fox, so they are women.
- The cardinal gets "maleT"; the high elf is slim, so he does not (same rule as Alain in Part 7).
- The mermaid and lamia use "full body" instead of "cowboy shot" so their tails show.
- Original designs, so there is no character tag; the description does all the work.
- Everyone is grown up: the body tags say "adult woman", "mature woman" or "adult man".
- DETAIL LEVEL: expanded. Every line now carries materials, small accessories, markings and effects.

//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
PART 4 | GENSHIN IMPACT: ADULT WOMEN | GI 01-60 | 60 prompts
//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
51 playable women up to Vesna and Vodyanitsa (September 2026), grouped by region, plus 9 story characters
(La Signora, the Tsaritsa, Rhinedottir, Alice, Focalors, Guizhong, Makoto, Kitsune Saiguu, Katheryne).
Each look was checked against the official wish art (story characters: the game model, card or illustration
on the Genshin Impact Fandom wiki). The header line of each entry says which.

WHO IS LEFT OUT (adults only, no teens)
  Kids:        Klee, Qiqi, Diona, Sayu, Dori, Nahida, Yaoyao, Sigewinne, Kachina, Iansan, Aino, Prune
  Teens:       Amber, Barbara, Xiangling, Fischl, Noelle, Sucrose, Xinyan, Collei, Layla, Kirara, Lynette
  Borderline:  Traveler (Lumine), Mona, Hu Tao, Faruzan, Citlali, Lan Yan, Jahoda
               The game never gives their age and they are drawn young.
  No usable art: Manekina (only an icon), Egeria and Liloupar (murals only)

- Most anime models know the older characters by name; the description tags matter most for characters from
  2025-2026, which many models have not seen yet.
- Every prompt is the default outfit from the wish art. Delete the pose line's props (motorcycle, surfboard,
  robot, deer...) for a plain standing pose.
- DETAIL LEVEL: expanded. Design details were added only where the official look is well known; elsewhere the
  additions are materials, expression, pose and effects on what was already listed.

//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
PART 8 | STARDEW VALLEY: CHARACTERS | SV 01-54 | 54 prompts
//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
Every character through update 1.6: the 12 marriage candidates, the other 22 villagers, 12 other named
characters, and 8 creatures and extras (including Krobus's 1.6 trenchcoat disguise).
Looks were checked against each official portrait, then written up as an anime-style character.
- Models mostly know the 12 marriage candidates (and Krobus); for everyone else the description does the work.
- The portraits only show head and shoulders, so lower-body clothing is left out unless it is well known.
- Kids (Jas, Vincent, Leo), the elderly and the creatures use the shorter quality line. Kids get no body tags.
- Creatures use "no humans" instead of 1boy/1girl. The goblin and the witch keep 1boy/1girl.
- Adult men get "maleT"; slim men (Elliott, Sam, Sebastian...) and the elderly do not.
- Mr. and Mrs. Raccoon are generic raccoons (no portrait exists). The farmer is left out.
- DETAIL LEVEL: expanded. Design details were added only where the official look is well known; elsewhere the
  additions are materials, expression, pose and effects on what was already listed.
